title: Publish
objective: Export your report from the claim graph and defend each line, with every claim under the section its stamp names, every assumption listed as ASSUMED [A], every exclusion listed as NOT COVERED [N], every doubt kept as m of n, and every bound, version and statement hash printed. Then publish a bundle in which `statespace check` resolves every link and every hash.

blocks.md:
Your repo holds every claim you have minted since Project 00. Once published, your Core is a research artifact in its own right, whether or not it ever becomes part of a larger system. A stranger will read one report. What may its first page say?

Two questions first. The segments after this one answer both.

choice.prompt: Your Core holds claims stamped PROVED [P], MODEL-CHECKED [M] and TESTED [T]. Which first-page summary may the report print?

options.text: "The Core is verified."
options.why: A bare "verified" erases the bounds, the assumptions and the checkers. The report's vocabulary leaves it out.

options.text: "80% of its claims are proved."
options.why: A percentage across stamps counts MODEL-CHECKED [M] and TESTED [T] claims as unfinished PROVED [P] ones.

options.text: The claims by stamp, each with its qualifier, plus what is assumed and what is not covered, each linked to its lines.
options.why: The summary is the walk of the claim graph, shortened. It is never a score.

options.text: "All tests and proofs pass."
options.why: Pass or fail hides what each check established, and its bound.

choice.prompt: A claim has four doubts identified. Receipts eliminated two, and you accepted one with a written rationale. What does its doubt log show?

options.text: 2|4, naming the two that remain: one accepted, one active.
options.why: The log counts doubts eliminated out of doubts identified, and names the others.

options.text: 3|4, because accepting a doubt eliminates it.
options.why: Acceptance is a decision about a doubt that remains. It does not eliminate it.
The log is a count, not a probability, and it never becomes a percentage.

blocks.md: Here is one claim, followed through the report. CL-5.3 says that a hold eventually resolves under stated fairness. Its stamp is MODEL-CHECKED [M] with its constants, and the fairness is an assumption. So the report lists it under MODEL-CHECKED with the constants and "complete" or "partial". An ASSUMED entry records weak fairness on the system's actions, with its why. The starving lasso, SP-5.3 {{run:RUN-tlc-hold-lasso}}, appears among the specimens as the counterexample when the fairness is weakened. And because ER-8 cracked SEAM-8 (SP-8.6), the line shows the crack and the remedy you took, "state recovery as an assumption, and check with crashes on", with CL-8.4's recovery assumption under ASSUMED. None of this changes CL-5.3's stamp.

You do not write the report. You export it: `statespace export` walks your claim graph and places every claim, and `statespace check` then confirms that the walk followed the rules and that every stamp re-derives from its receipt. You write the propositions, the assumptions, the doubts and the limitations. The tool decides where each one goes.

The export writes these sections, in this order: a title block with the edition pins, the commit and the bundle hash, and no claim about who you are; what this report establishes and what it does not (CL-10.2); the Core and its trusted base; the operational semantics and your four decision records; the theorem statements with their hashes; PROVED; MODEL-CHECKED; TESTED; ENFORCED; CONFIGURED; ASSUMED; NOT COVERED; UNKNOWN; the specimens; the demonstration (CL-10.1); the erosion log; the doubt log; the checker matrix; the budgets and advisories; the agent incident ledger; the known limitations; and how to reproduce it.

Twelve rules govern the walk, and `statespace check report/` confirms each one.

| Rule | The report must |
|---|---|
| T1 | Put each claim once in the stamp sections, under its proposition-of-model stamp. REFUTED [R] results live with the specimens. |
| T2 | Print each line's stamp word, code and qualifier (the bound first for MODEL-CHECKED [M] and TESTED [T]), its label for where it was checked, its statement hash, its receipt ids and its three-segment strip. Requirement-fit is never PROVED [P]. |
| T3 | Turn each rests-on edge into an ASSUMED entry with its why, and each NOT COVERED [N] line into a NOT COVERED entry. |
| T4 | List the parts of a composite claim and give it no single stamp, least of all its strongest part's. |
| T5 | Move a claim whose statement hash no longer matches, or whose receipt fails re-verification, to UNKNOWN [?] with the reason. Nothing is dropped. |
| T6 | Keep a cracked claim's stamp and show the crack and the remedy. List every erosion in the log with both endpoints, its forecast result and its remedy. |
| T7 | Write "PROVED modulo k assumed lemmas", in words, when a Lean claim has k parked goals. Each lemma sits under ASSUMED with its parked date. |
| T8 | Print no bare "verified", "correct" or "safe", and no sum, average or percentage of stamps or of doubt counts. |
| T9 | Put design-level MODEL-CHECKED [M] claims and implementation-level TESTED [T] claims side by side, cross-linked, never merged. |
| T10 | Give the checker matrix one row per claim and one column per checker. Each cell is a verdict line with its receipt id, or blank. Nothing is inferred. |
| T11 | Print every bound and every tool version, with the advisories known on the report's date and each receipt's age limit, "stale since" once it has passed. |
| T12 | List every triaged proposal in the agent incident ledger: date, seed, operator family, verdict, class named and decision. |

The cell shows one record from a claim graph and asks you where the exporter puts it.

blocks.direction: `statespace export` reads this record from the claim graph and places it in the report. The cell shows the record, and the call is where it lands.

code.text:
claim         CL-6.2
proposition   the conditional-UPDATE compilation never overspends
              under concurrent READ COMMITTED
stamp         TESTED [T] · n histories · the search bound
rests on      [A] PostgreSQL behaves as documented

call.prompt: CL-6.2, "the conditional-UPDATE compilation never overspends under concurrent READ COMMITTED", is TESTED [T] · n histories, plus one ASSUMED [A] clause. Where does the exporter put it?

options.text: Under TESTED with n and the search bound, plus one ASSUMED entry for the clause.
options.why: Rules T1 and T3: the claim goes under the stamp its proposition earns, and each assumption becomes an entry of its own.

options.text: Under PROVED: the executed runs show no lost update.
options.why: Recorded histories are tests {{run:RUN-pg-anomalies}}, and no run covers every history.

options.text: Under ASSUMED only: it depends on PostgreSQL.
options.why: Its proposition was tested. The dependence sits beside it, not instead of it.

options.text: Under TESTED, with its assumptions in a footnote.
options.why: An assumption that is not an entry cannot be counted, cracked or audited.

blocks.after: The exporter puts CL-6.2 once, under TESTED, with n and the search bound printed (rule T1), and it creates an ASSUMED entry for the clause, with its why (rule T3). A claim keeps its section when it has assumptions. They get entries of their own, where they can be counted, cracked and audited {{run:RUN-core-demo}}.

choice.prompt: A claim-graph fragment holds CL-5.1 (MODEL-CHECKED [M], complete), CL-6.2 (TESTED [T], with one ASSUMED [A] clause) and the composite CL-10.1. Which statement about its report is true?

options.text: CL-10.1 appears under PROVED, the stamp of its strongest part.
options.why: A composite takes no single stamp (T4), least of all its strongest part's.

options.text: CL-5.1 appears once, under MODEL-CHECKED with its constants and "complete", and each assumption it rests on has an ASSUMED entry.
options.why: Rules T1 and T3.

options.text: CL-6.2 moves to UNKNOWN because a seam under it cracked.
options.why: An erosion cracks a segment or an assumption record, never silently the proposition. The claim keeps its stamp and shows the crack and the remedy (T6).

options.text: "The requirement-fit segment of a claim may read PROVED [P] when its proposition does."
options.why: Requirement-fit is never PROVED [P]. It carries your requirement scenarios as tests or assumptions (T2).

blocks.md:
A doubt is a reason why a claim might not hold. A claim with no doubts listed is not a claim without doubts. It is a claim nobody has looked at. The report keeps a doubt log for every claim, and the log has a shape.

There are three kinds of doubt, and they match the Audit Desk's gap classes. A rebutting doubt says the claim is false, and it comes as a counterexample. An undermining doubt says the evidence cannot be trusted: the solver, the encoding, the tool. An undercutting doubt says the reasoning from evidence to claim fails. Each doubt is active, retired, or an accepted residual. The log reads m|n: n doubts identified, m of them retired, and the other n − m named, active ones first.

Nine rules decide what happens to a doubt.

| Rule | What it says |
|---|---|
| D1 | Only a linked specimen, receipt or written argument retires a doubt. An AI may propose a doubt, labeled as its proposal, and never retires one. |
| D2 | A doubt that is not retired is active, unless you accept it as a residual, with a written rationale. |
| D3 | An argument is open while any doubt is active, or while any assumption it rests on reaches an unsupported claim or a crack with no remedy. Otherwise it is closed. |
| D4 | The log reads m|n, with the n − m others named. It is never summed, averaged, ranked or gated on. |
| D5 | An agreeing second checker retires a one-checker doubt and opens a doubt that both could fail together. An agreeing independent oracle retires a doubt about the specification only within its generator's distribution, and opens one for what lies outside it. |
| D6 | An erosion opens a doubt of the seam's kind on every claim that rests on the seam. The remedy retires it or restates it as a new assumption. |
| D7 | An advisory newer than a receipt opens a re-check doubt on every claim that cites that tool version. A receipt on a fixed version retires it. |
| D8 | A dismissed doubt keeps its record and rationale, and counts as retired only under D1. |
| D9 | The published report, CL-10.2, carries one standing doubt, "doubts not yet identified", accepted with a rationale that records the checklist you ran. It is never retired. |

To hunt doubts, go through every inference rule for undercutting doubts, every item of evidence for undermining ones, and every claim for counterexamples (Goodenough, Weinstock and Klein, 2015, section 3.1). The seven-category checklist from Gohar and colleagues' study of doubts in real safety cases is a good second pass.

Here is CL-1.1's doubt log, before the cross-check.

| # | Doubt | Kind | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The premises may contradict each other | Undercutting | Retired by receipt: the premise witness is satisfiable (LAB-1.c3) |
| 2 | The unsat rests on one solver | Undermining | Active. SEAM-7 cracked at ER-7 through SP-4.5, where an earlier Z3 release gave a wrong answer on two satisfiable inputs and the pinned release gives no verdict on them {{run:RUN-z3-11179}} |
| 3 | The recipient can overflow in 64-bit arithmetic | Undermining | Accepted residual, listed under NOT COVERED with CL-1.5's line |

The log reads 1|3. Now import the cvc5 cross-check receipt for the same query.

blocks.direction: The receipt is imported and linked to the doubt it answers. The course's tool recomputes CL-1.1's log under the nine rules.

code.text:
import   receipt for CL-1.1's query, from the cvc5 cross-check
claim    CL-1.1
before   1|3
event    the receipt is linked to doubt 2

call.prompt: What happens to doubt 2, "the unsat rests on one solver"?

options.text: It is retired, and the claim's argument closes.
options.why: Agreement answers the one-solver doubt, but two solvers can fail together. A new doubt about that opens and keeps the argument open.

options.text: It stays active: a proof with a `hole` proves nothing.
options.why: The `hole` limits the certificate, not cvc5's independent answer.

options.text: It is deleted: the newer release of Z3 no longer gives the wrong answer.
options.why: Doubts are never deleted, and a changed answer on one input establishes no soundness.

options.text: It is retired by the receipt, and a new doubt opens: "both solvers could be wrong, and the certificate is incomplete". The new doubt is active until you accept it with a rationale.
options.why: Rules D1 and D5. The log reads 2|4, and checking a certificate is a deferred drawer (D-32).

blocks.after: The receipt retires doubt 2 (rule D1), because an independent solver gave the same answer. Rule D5 opens a doubt that both solvers could be wrong. The proof cvc5 wrote is 19 lines long and holds 3 `hole` steps, where a rewrite was not translated, so the certificate is incomplete {{run:RUN-cvc5-alethe}}. The log now reads 2|4. Doubts 3 and 4 are the two that remain: one accepted, one active.

choice.prompt: An advisory for the Z3 version that your receipt for CL-4.4 names is published after the receipt's date, and the claim's doubt log gains an entry. What status does that doubt hold?

options.text: Retired: the receipt is older than the advisory, so it predates the problem.
options.why: Only a linked specimen, receipt or written argument retires a doubt (D1), and the receipt is the thing in doubt.

options.text: Active: nothing yet shows the receipt is unaffected, and a receipt on a fixed version would retire it.
options.why: Rule D7 opens a re-check doubt on every claim that cites the tool version, and it stays active until something linked retires it.

options.text: Accepted residual: an advisory is a rationale of its own.
options.why: Accepting a doubt takes your own written rationale (D2). An advisory is not one.

blocks.md:
A line in your report is reproducible only if a stranger can run it again and compare. So a receipt carries the tool and its version, the binary's hash, the argv, the hash of each input, the bound or seed, and the statement hash. Leave one out and the line says what you saw, not what anyone else can see.

The statement hash is what catches edits. It covers the statement's text with trailing whitespace removed, plus one newline, which matches the challenge hash of Comparator Live. A claim whose hash no longer matches, or whose receipt fails re-verification, moves to UNKNOWN [?] with the reason, and stays visible.

Receipts age. Each one carries a time to live, and past it the report prints "stale since". An advisory newer than a receipt opens a re-check doubt on every claim that cites the tool version.

The course pins the editions it recorded runs on: Lean 4.35.0 and PostgreSQL 18.6. The PostgreSQL catalog is re-recorded after the next major release. Your report prints the editions you ran.

Write limitations in the open, as NOT COVERED lines for what lies outside and ASSUMED lines for what you depend on. CompCert's manual draws the same line between what its proof covers and what it does not (chapter 1, sections 1.2 and 1.3). Here is a finished line, from executed runs.

> CL-5.1 · MODEL-CHECKED [M] · constants Init = 100, Amount = 80, Workers = {w1, w2} · complete · 4 distinct states · TLC build 2026.10.20.183001 (rev: d2e1472), jar pinned by SHA-256, pre-release · argv recorded · statement hash printed {{run:RUN-tlc-jars}}. Also run at three workers with Amount = 40: 8 distinct states {{run:RUN-tlc-atomic}}. Other sizes: NOT COVERED, unless the parametric step of CL-5.4 is proved.

Before you publish, `statespace check bundle/` also runs a privacy check: no private paths, secrets or identifiers that you did not choose to publish, and nothing from your private overlay. The bundle names the artifact and never you. Where to publish is your choice, and the check runs on the local bundle.

An agent commit has weakened the statement of `transfer_conserves`, under the same name, and `statespace check` has run comparator again.

blocks.direction: The commit builds, because the weaker statement is true and its proof is complete. `statespace check` then compares the solution's statement with the pinned one, theorem by theorem, and the report is exported again.

code.text:
-- the pinned statement
theorem transfer_conserves (s : Ledger) (n : Int) :
    total (transfer s n) = total s

-- the agent's commit: the same name, one more hypothesis
theorem transfer_conserves (s : Ledger) (n : Int) (h : n = 0) :
    total (transfer s n) = total s := by
  subst h; unfold transfer total; split <;> simp

call.prompt: Where does CL-2.1 appear in the re-exported report?

options.text: Under PROVED: the proof still builds.
options.why: The build proves the weakened statement, not the pinned one.

options.text: Under REFUTED: the statement changed.
options.why: REFUTED [R] needs a witness that violates the claim. Nothing was refuted.

options.text: Under UNKNOWN, with the reason "statement mismatch", until the pinned statement is proved again.
options.why: A statement mismatch voids the claim to UNKNOWN [?], and rule T5 keeps it visible.

options.text: Nowhere: voided claims are dropped.
options.why: Dropping it would hide exactly the edit that comparator caught.

blocks.after: Comparator rejects the solution, because the statement does not match the pinned one {{run:RUN-lean-comparator}}. The build of the weakened theorem is still green: the kernel accepted a different statement. In the report, CL-2.1 moves to UNKNOWN [?] with the reason "statement mismatch", and it stays visible until the pinned statement is proved again (rule T5).

choice.prompt: A report line reads: "CL-5.1 · MODEL-CHECKED [M] · complete · argv recorded". Which element of its qualifier is missing?

options.text: The checker and its version.
options.why: That belongs to PROVED [P]. MODEL-CHECKED [M] names its constants and whether the check was complete or partial.

options.text: The number of runs and the generator's statistics.
options.why: That belongs to TESTED [T]. A model check is not a sample.

options.text: The constants the check ran with.
options.why: MODEL-CHECKED [M] needs its constants beside "complete". A result about two workers says nothing about three.

options.text: A why.
options.why: A why belongs to ASSUMED [A].

choice.prompt: Which report line is reproducible as written?

options.text: "CL-4.2 · PROVED [P] · Z3 said unsat."
options.why: It has no version, no budget and no statement hash.

options.text: "CL-6.1 · TESTED [T] · n sequences · no divergence."
options.why: It has no seed, no generator statistics and no engine versions.

options.text: "CL-2.1 · PROVED [P] · the build is green."
options.why: A green build is not a checker's verdict, and the line carries no statement hash or axiom list.

options.text: "CL-5.1 · MODEL-CHECKED [M] · constants and complete printed · TLC version and jar hash recorded · argv recorded · statement hash printed."
options.why: Tool, version, binary hash, argv, constants and statement hash are all there, so a stranger can run it again and compare.

choice.prompt: A doubt on CL-1.5, "the recipient can wrap in 64-bit arithmetic", is active. You write that the doubt applies, that the claim does not cover 64-bit wrap, and that you accept this, and you add the NOT COVERED line. What is the doubt's status now?

options.text: Retired: you answered it in writing.
options.why: The doubt still applies. Accepting it is not answering it.

options.text: Active: nothing linked has retired it.
options.why: Accepting a doubt with a written rationale moves it out of active (D2). It stays in the log.

options.text: Accepted residual.
options.why: The doubt remains, you have written why you accept it, and the log still names it.

choice.prompt: Which segment of a claim's three-segment strip never reads PROVED [P]?

options.text: Proposition-of-model.
options.why: A proof of the proposition in its model earns PROVED [P] there.

options.text: Correspondence.
options.why: A preservation proof can earn PROVED [P] there, as in CL-9.2.

options.text: Requirement-fit.
options.why: Whether the claim is what you needed is carried by your scenarios as tests or assumptions, and never by a proof.

options.text: None: any segment may.
options.why: Requirement-fit is the exception, because a proof is about its statement and not about your intent.

blocks.md: These ideas return in Today as placement questions, doubt statuses, and report lines to complete or to judge as reproducible. When an advisory lands for a tool version that one of your receipts names, Today shows it as a change to check.

blocks.title: Production twin: Cedar's release evidence
blocks.md: Read Cedar's release gate as release evidence. At the pinned `cedar-spec` commit in {{run:RUN-twin-pins}}, sort the properties the README lists into proved in Lean, tested by differential testing, and trusted. Then list what the gate re-runs before a release.

blocks.title: Build this
